title: What Does "Now" Mean to Your Computer-Use Agent? Stale Screenshots, Page Loads, and Which Check to Run Before a Click
abstract: arXiv:2610.39282v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Computer-use agents plan on a screenshot for several seconds and then click at a position on the screen; if the page has changed in the meantime, the click lands on an unintended element. Prior work treats the planning interval as the source of this risk. Measuring planned clicks on 31 public web pages, we find that the risk lies in page loading: 0.4% of clicks planned on fully loaded pages became stale within 30 seconds, against 17% of clicks planned in the first second after a page opened. On these pages, waiting about one second for network activity to stop removes most of this risk, yet the wait rules of eight of ten widely used open-source agents leave more than 1% of clicks stale. Commercial pages keep loading for longer: in the HTTP Archive's public crawl, 15% of 65 desktop booking and buying home pages went 500 ms without network requests within 3 seconds of their HTML being parsed, against 63% of 3,028 .gov pages, and 52% shifte

translated_title: “现在”对您的计算机使用智能体意味着什么？过时的屏幕截图、页面加载，以及点击前应运行哪种检查
translated_abstract: 计算机使用智能体会基于屏幕截图进行数秒的规划，然后点击屏幕上的某个位置；如果在此期间页面发生了变化，点击就会落在非预期的元素上。先前的工作将规划时间间隔视为这种风险的来源。通过测量31个公开网页上的计划点击，我们发现真正的风险在于页面加载：在完全加载的页面上规划的点击中，仅有0.4%在30秒内变得过时，而在页面打开后第一秒内规划的点击中，这一比例高达17%。在这些页面上，等待约一秒钟直到网络活动停止即可消除大部分风险，然而十个广泛使用的开源智能体中，有八个的等待规则会导致超过1%的点击过时。商业页面持续加载的时间更长：在HTTP Archive的公开抓取数据中，65个桌面端预订和购买类主页中有15%在HTML解析后的3秒内出现500毫秒无网络请求的情况，而3,028个.gov页面中这一比例为63%，并且52%的页面发生了偏移（原文摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该研究发现计算机使用智能体点击失效的主要风险来自页面加载而非规划延迟——页面打开后第一秒内规划的点击有17%会过时，而完全加载的页面上这一比例仅为0.4%——等待约一秒让网络活动停止即可消除大部分风险，但十个主流开源智能体中有八个的等待规则未能做到这一点。
en_tdlr: This study finds that the main risk of stale clicks for computer-use agents lies in page loading rather than planning delay—17% of clicks planned within the first second after a page opens become stale versus only 0.4% on fully loaded pages—and waiting about one second for network activity to stop removes most of this risk, yet eight of ten widely used open-source agents' wait rules fail to achieve this.
